contract: Musoq Search completion and budget contract
implementationStatus: W12-S01 implements the terminal accounting model and source-side summary for file-backed text Search sources. SQL terminal-summary transport and consumer delivery remain owned by W12-S02 and later scopes.

terminalSummary.delivery: exactly one terminal summary after observed rows, or as the first and only result when no rows exist
terminalSummary.zeroRows: A zero-row query still delivers the summary; absence of occurrence rows is never evidence of success by itself.
terminalSummary.rowCompleteness: Do not put IsComplete on occurrence rows; consumers use the terminal summary and reject Failed or unapproved Partial prefixes.

QuerySatisfied.meaning: An explicit positive or limited query demand was met before the whole eligible scope was processed.

ScopeExhausted.meaning: Every eligible input was processed, or every excluded input was excluded by the declared scope policy, so a negative answer is bounded by the recorded scope.

Failed.meaning: No successful complete answer can be accepted; retain a typed cause and any observed prefix only as rejected evidence under strict policy.

Partial.meaning: An explicit partial-results policy permits delivery of observed evidence, but a limit or failure prevented the complete contract.

invariants: QuerySatisfied does not imply ScopeExhausted; TAKE is a query limit, not a scan budget.
ScopeExhausted is the only outcome that can claim an exhaustive negative answer.
Failed and Partial are never silently converted to an empty or successful result.
A terminal summary is delivered exactly once even when no occurrence row exists.
Every terminal outcome includes a stable reason; failures include a typed code and path when applicable.
A live filesystem is not an atomic snapshot merely because traversal reached its end.

fullInput.meaning: Validate the complete request and each candidate file's required classification before that file's rows are eligible for emission.
fullInput.lateFailure: A late binary marker or decode failure is resolved before rows from that file are accepted; a declared skip remains visible in the terminal summary.
fullInput.scopeClaim: A successful exhaustive result may claim ScopeExhausted only after all eligible candidates finish under this mode.

observedPrefix.meaning: An explicitly selected streaming policy may emit evidence from the observed prefix before the complete file is validated.
observedPrefix.lateFailure: A failure discovered after emission produces Failed under strict policy or Partial only under explicit partial policy; already emitted evidence is never retracted invisibly.
observedPrefix.scopeClaim: Observed-prefix validation can never claim ScopeExhausted for an unfinished candidate.

requestRules: Request and option validation is complete before opening the root.
A prefix count is exact only for observed rows; it is not an exact total for the scope.
Terminal summary delivery is required for both validation modes.

principles: A budget exhaustion is a named terminal reason, not a successful truncation.
TAKE limits requested output cardinality and may yield QuerySatisfied; it does not make the scan exhaustive.
Output, read, file, elapsed-time and in-flight budgets are work or delivery limits and fail strictly by default.
An explicit partial policy may preserve an observed prefix as Partial, never as ScopeExhausted or QuerySatisfied.

limits.name: take
limits.whenReached: QuerySatisfied with terminalReason=take-reached when the requested positive/limited result has been produced

limits.name: output-cap
limits.whenReachedPartial: Partial with terminalReason=budget-exhausted and failureCode=output-cap when partialPolicy=allow and observedRows>0

limits.name: read-bytes
limits.whenReached: Failed or explicit-policy Partial; never ScopeExhausted

limits.name: files
limits.whenReached: Failed or explicit-policy Partial; do not call the unvisited suffix exhausted

limits.name: elapsed-time
limits.whenReached: Failed or explicit-policy Partial with failureCode=timeout

exactness.ScopeExhausted: scope and match counters are exact for the resolved execution, subject to the non-atomic filesystem qualification
exactness.QuerySatisfied: emitted/observed prefix counters are exact; total scope and occurrence counters are not exact
exactness.Failed: counters are observed-prefix measurements only and cannot support a negative answer
exactness.Partial: counters describe retained evidence only and cannot support a negative answer

counters.unknownRoot: Missing or inaccessible roots do not masquerade as zero eligible files; scopeResolved and countsExact remain false.

binaryPolicy.classification: A binary marker observed within the declared probe or during full-input validation is a scope decision, not an invisible success.
binaryPolicy.lateMarker: Under observed-prefix validation, a marker after emitted rows is a terminal failure/partial event and cannot retract those rows invisibly.
binaryPolicy.summary: binaryFilesSkipped and the decision reason are included in the terminal summary and scope evidence.

zeroMatchOutcomes.answer: The declared scope contains no eligible files; this is a complete zero result, not a missing-root result.

zeroMatchOutcomes.condition: scopeResolved=true, eligibleFiles>0 and all eligible files complete with occurrences=0
zeroMatchOutcomes.answer: No occurrence exists in the processed eligible scope.

zeroMatchOutcomes.condition: all binary files are excluded by the explicit skip-and-report policy and the scope completes
zeroMatchOutcomes.answer: No match is reported for the policy-selected text scope; binaryFilesSkipped makes the exclusion visible.
